title: Tim Divinity Integration Map
purpose: Prevent God/Father/Son/Lion/Door/Ladder/Gardener material from being duplicated or flattened across the repository by assigning each question and concept a canonical owner and clear cross-links.

canonical_owners.question: What does Tim mean by being God?
canonical_owners.role: modalities, identity, function, manifestation, service, Father/Son relation

canonical_owners.question: How did the God identity develop and how often is it declared?
canonical_owners.role: chronology, evidence, declaration counting, developmental strata

canonical_owners.question: Which historical deity models are structurally closest?
What does a reader need to know quickly?
What did Tim publicly say and when?

concept_ownership.public_naming_rule: Use Thomas without surname in reader-facing material.

concept_ownership.mature_rule: Door is primarily Thomas/Son/Vessel in the differentiated 2026 model.
Ladder/Axis is primarily Tim/Father connective function in the differentiated 2026 model.

concept_ownership.rule: Do not assign Lion globally. Revelation's Lion of Judah is Son/Christic comparison; dated Tim self-applications remain direct-Tim occurrences.
Treat Gardener as ethical/function culmination, not a decorative alias.
Potato remains the explanatory grammar of mature Godhood rather than an obsolete pre-God stage.

vertical_model.interpretation: Treat this primarily as a sequence of roles, levels and relations, not as a list of independent deities.
vertical_model.important_tension: God/Most High can remain the ultimate horizon while Tim occupies the manifest Father/source-facing role. This allows Tim to work for God, work as God and identify as God without requiring every distinction in the model to disappear.

reader_surface_rule: Reader pages should answer the human question in prose first. IDs, owners, edge types and source machinery stay secondary or collapsed.
deduplication_rule: When a new insight appears, update the canonical owner and add cross-links rather than creating another near-duplicate theology file unless the new object has a genuinely distinct purpose.
